note:
Cavendish Crescent North on the 1901 census - the little of this round the existing files do not hold.

**Four households are covered already** - Hardwicke House, Haddon House, Cavendish Lodge and most of Carisbrooke House - and are not repeated.

**What is new is one household and two empty houses.** Schedule 192 gives **Doyley Scott Ransom**, a solicitor of 38, his wife Helen, four small daughters including a niece and a baby of six months, and four servants. The page carries no house name or number, so it is unfiled.

**Peveril House and Blantyre both stood empty on census night**, which is why the crescent looks thinner in 1901 than its property list suggests. They are recorded in [[empty-houses-census-night-1901]] and carry no household here.

**Anyone already written into another 1901 file is left out of this one.** Most of these households are part done - the existing files hold the head and some of the servants but not the children, or the other way about - so the skipping is person by person rather than household by household, and what remains is only what no committed file already carries.
source: 1901 census enumerator's page for Cavendish Crescent North, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
